prompt_en: A frontal photograph of one freestanding wooden R bookend on a base, with complete stem, upper bowl and down-right leg. Its counter is a complete left-arrow negative shape with a broad shaft and triangular head, revealing the light background. Do not turn the outer leg left or print a separate surface arrow instead.

Frontal product photograph of a rigid luggage tag bearing a broad B with cut-through counters. Its upper counter is a right-arrow cutout and lower counter a left-arrow cutout, each with a complete head and shaft revealing the background. The outer upper bowl is narrower than the lower bowl. Do not invert the B or substitute printed arrows inside solid counters.

A frontal photograph of a narrow upright shop sign bearing an NN ligature. The Ns share one middle upright, giving three equal-height verticals in total. The two outer uprights are thick; the middle upright and both descending diagonals are thin. Each diagonal runs from the upper-left to lower-right between neighboring uprights. Do not add a fourth upright or make all strokes equally thick.

A frontal photograph of a square door plaque carrying a TH monogram. H’s left and right uprights extend above and below one shared horizontal bar. T’s central stem extends only downward from that same bar. The whole mark has one horizontal and three vertical strokes. Do not extend the middle stem above the bar. No explanatory letter labels.

Frontal photograph of one metal AB bookshop monogram. A’s right diagonal leg is exactly the same slanted stem used by B. B’s two bowls lie to its right and join the stem at top, midpoint and bottom. A’s crossbar meets the same shared member. Do not add a separate upright B stem.

A frontal photograph of an ivory dessert name card in a pastry display, with large dark text on two lines: CRÈME and BRÛLÉE. The È has a grave accent leaning upper-left, Û an upward-pointing circumflex, and É an acute accent leaning upper-right. No translation or price. Do not replace the different accents with identical horizontal strokes.

A frontal close photograph of a textbook line reading a < b ≤ c ≠ d. The first less-than sign has no lower bar; the less-than-or-equal sign has one lower bar; the not-equal sign has a slash across its two horizontals. Letters share one baseline. No calculation result or explanation.

A frontal close photograph of a calculus workbook showing one large expression: f prime of x, plus f double-prime of x, equals x squared. The first f has one prime at upper right; the second has two. After the equals sign, the 2 is a superscript numeral, not two prime strokes. Keep symbols distinct, without a solution or explanation.

A frontal photograph of one parking-entrance sign stand with two clear signs. The blue sign has only a large white P. The white sign has a large black P inside a red ring, crossed by one red slash from upper left to lower right. Keep both signs separate and complete. Do not add the slash to the blue sign or remove it from the white one. No other text.

A frontal photograph of one dark-green metal coffee-shop sign reading MORROW. M, both Os and W use solid ivory letter strokes. The adjacent Rs differ: the first R is an outline letter, with thin ivory contours enclosing dark-green stroke interiors; the second R has solid ivory strokes. Keep the letters separate and similar in size, with their normal counters readable. Do not outline the whole word or fill the first R solid.

A frontal close photograph of a microwave display reading End in clear illuminated segmented characters. E uses both left verticals and top, middle and bottom horizontals. n uses the middle horizontal and the two lower verticals only. d uses upper-right, lower-right and lower-left verticals plus middle and bottom horizontals. All other segments are dark. Do not substitute continuous printed letters or add time digits.

A frontal photograph of an electronic film clapperboard with one large timecode display reading 01:02:03;04. The first two separators are colons; the last is a semicolon. Its black-and-white hinged clapper is closed above the display. Keep the timecode unobstructed, without a date, second number display or explanation text.

Frontal photograph of a flat sports jersey with one large navy 8. Its two white counters are not ellipses: the upper is a complete white 6 and the lower a complete white 9, each with a navy inner eye. The upper 6 tail reaches upper-right; the lower 9 tail reaches lower-left. Keep the outer 8 loops equally wide. No separate 69 lettering.

A frontal close photograph of one three-digit physical seven-segment sports scoreboard displaying 286. Use standard seven-segment digit shapes. In 2 and 8, every lit horizontal segment is warm white and every lit vertical segment is amber. In 6, the lit horizontals are amber and the lit verticals are warm white. Unlit segments are dark against the black face, with no glow. Make the digits large and segment gaps clear, and show no additional score.

A frontal photograph of a music-player remote with four large buttons. Their icons are: one filled right triangle; two separate vertical bars; two adjacent filled right triangles; and one filled right triangle with a separate vertical bar to its right. Each icon occurs once; button layout is unrestricted. Use clear black-and-white icons without text or other function buttons.

A near-frontal close photograph of the left side of a keyboard with two prominent large keys carrying icons only. Shift has an outlined upward arrow with no bar beneath its shaft. Caps Lock has an outlined upward arrow plus a separate short solid horizontal bar below the shaft. Keep both icons upright and complete on natural keycaps, with no explanatory icons or text outside the keys.

A frontal photograph of a dark wooden chair whose broad backrest contains one complete lightning-bolt cutout revealing the light wall behind it. The bolt has a broad upper part, a middle zigzag return and a pointed lower end, not a plain triangle. Keep the backrest outer edge intact and show wood thickness at the opening. Do not substitute a printed bolt on the surface. Normal seat and legs.

Frontal close photograph of a game controller’s large cross-shaped directional pad. One separate white arrow per arm: top points down, left points left, right points left, bottom points up. No arrow connections or direction words; do not make all four arrows point outward.

A frontal photograph of one custom dark-blue restaurant wayfinding plaque on an ivory wall. Its physical outer silhouette is a broad left-pointing arrow with a clear shaft and triangular head. Inside the shaft is one complete right-pointing arrow cutout revealing the ivory wall, with a visible shaft and triangular head. The two directions oppose, with a generous blue border between the inner and outer contours. No lettering and no second adjacent plaque.

A frontal photograph of a square transport-museum direction sign. The top bar of a large T is also the shaft of a right arrow, with one triangular head at its right end. T’s stem descends from the bar midpoint. There is only one long horizontal shaft. Do not add a separate arrow beside T or put the head on the bottom of the stem.

A natural photograph of one teamwear care worktable. Show all specified working faces prominently and completely in one coherent environment, with no mutual occlusion or separate answer panels. One laid-flat sports jersey bears a custom AR ligature emblem on its chest. A is left and R right, sharing exactly one central upright. A’s left leg slopes up to its top; A’s right leg is that upright, with a crossbar meeting its midpoint. R’s closed upper bowl bulges right from the same upright’s upper half; its diagonal leg runs down-right from the shared midpoint. Not two separately typeset letters or a doubled central stem. one broad sewn clothing-care label with three large symbols stacked compactly. Top: navy square outline on ivory, enclosing a full circle and one central dot. Middle: ivory circle on a solid navy square, with two separated ivory dots inside. Bottom: navy square outline on ivory enclosing one horizontal line, no circle or dots. Complete symbols, no text.

A natural photograph of one school clothing preparation table. Show all specified working faces prominently and completely in one coherent environment, with no mutual occlusion or separate answer panels. One child’s backpack has one large embroidered weather badge. An ivory cloud covers the lower part of a gold sun; the exposed upper sun has exactly three separate short rays. Three separate blue raindrops sit below the cloud. One continuous cloud shape, no lightning, snowflakes or crescent. Sun, cloud and rain belong to one badge, not three separate patches. one broad sewn clothing-care label with three large symbols stacked compactly. Top: navy square outline on ivory, enclosing a full circle and one central dot. Middle: ivory circle on a solid navy square, with two separated ivory dots inside. Bottom: navy square outline on ivory enclosing one horizontal line, no circle or dots. Complete symbols, no text.

Close frontal photograph of one broad sewn clothing-care label with three large symbols stacked compactly. Top: navy square outline on ivory, enclosing a full circle and one central dot. Middle: ivory circle on a solid navy square, with two separated ivory dots inside. Bottom: navy square outline on ivory enclosing one horizontal line, no circle or dots. Complete symbols, no text.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. On a family cafe shelf, a single complete metal-outline word sculpture reads MOM upright and WOW when the same sculpture is turned upside down. The middle O is a rectangular loop whose left and right sides also serve as the rightmost upright of the left M and the leftmost upright of the right M. Do not duplicate these shared uprights. Each M has upright outer stems and a central downward valley. No second answer line accompanies the sculpture.

A frontal photograph of a large-print three-note staff exercise. All three filled noteheads share the same height and have upward stems. Before the left head is a natural sign, before the middle a flat, and before the right a sharp. Leave clear space between each accidental and its notehead. Do not turn the natural sign into a hash. No other notes or text.

A frontal close photograph of a large-print practice score on a piano music stand. A single five-line staff carries six separated notes left to right. Counting staff lines upward from the bottom, place their noteheads on the bottom line, in the first space, on the third line, in the third space, on the fifth line, and in the fourth space. The second and fifth heads are hollow; the others are filled. Each has its own upward stem, without flags, beams, text or extra notes. Use fine staff lines and large clear noteheads.

A frontal close photograph of a large-print music score with four noteheads left to right on the same staff line. The first two are filled, with upward stems joined by one thick straight beam at the stem tops. The last two are filled with independent upward stems and no beam; one fine curved tie joins them below the noteheads. Separate the two groups. No extra heads, flags or text.

A frontal close photograph of one wide five-line staff with repeat signs at both ends. At the left start-repeat sign, a thick vertical bar is leftmost, a thin bar follows, and two dots are to their right. At the right end-repeat sign, two dots precede a thin bar and a thick rightmost bar. Each dot pair occupies the second and third staff spaces. Leave the middle staff empty, without notes or text.

Frontal close photograph of one music-practice measure with five clear horizontal staff lines and four separate solid oval noteheads. Left to right: second line from bottom, third line, space between bottom and second line, fourth line. First and fourth stems rise from the right sides of their heads and alone join one slightly descending-right beam. Second and third stems descend from the left sides, each with one individual flag, not joined to that upper beam. No clef, text or other notes.

A frontal close photograph of two wheeled recycling bins standing side by side. Both have a closed attached lid and one large three-arrow recycling emblem printed directly on the front. The left emblem flows clockwise and the right counterclockwise. Each has exactly three separated broad curved arrows, one head and one blunt tail per arrow, without forks, duplicate heads or a detached sign board. Keep both complete bin fronts visible, with no rubbish obscuring the emblems.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. A household sorting bin has one recycling emblem on its flat lid. Three broad arrows all run clockwise around a triangular loop. The upper-right arrow is solid dark green; the bottom and upper-left arrows are thick dark-green outlines with the lid color visible inside. Short visible gaps separate each head from the next tail. Do not fill the outlined arrows or add a fourth arrow.

A frontal photograph of a public recycling bin with one large three-arrow recycling emblem. The arrows chase clockwise around a triangle. The upper arrow is entirely blue and the other two entirely white. Each arrow’s shaft, bend and triangular head share its color, with clear gaps between arrows. Do not split an arrow into two colors based on image left and right. No other emblem or text.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. A spread-out team jersey bears one large embroidered MR monogram. M is left and R is right. The rightmost stem of M is the only upright of R, with no doubled middle stems. R has a closed upper bowl and a diagonal leg running from the middle of the shared stem down-right. The middle of M is a downward V, not a horizontal bar. Broad, clear embroidered strokes.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. A matte insulated flask has one large navy circular brand emblem on its broad front. A pale leaf is cut out of the navy field, pointing up-right. A navy main vein runs continuously from the lower-left petiole into the leaf but stops short of the tip. Two short diagonal side veins join the main vein on its right side, none on its left. Do not fill the whole leaf navy.

A natural photograph of one sports travel-packing table. Show all specified working faces prominently and completely in one coherent environment, with no mutual occlusion or separate answer panels. One laid-flat sports jersey bears a custom AR ligature emblem on its chest. A is left and R right, sharing exactly one central upright. A’s left leg slopes up to its top; A’s right leg is that upright, with a crossbar meeting its midpoint. R’s closed upper bowl bulges right from the same upright’s upper half; its diagonal leg runs down-right from the shared midpoint. Not two separately typeset letters or a doubled central stem. One child’s backpack has one large embroidered weather badge. An ivory cloud covers the lower part of a gold sun; the exposed upper sun has exactly three separate short rays. Three separate blue raindrops sit below the cloud. One continuous cloud shape, no lightning, snowflakes or crescent. Sun, cloud and rain belong to one badge, not three separate patches.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. A square tea tin has one large two-color brand ring on its front. Its outer ring is navy, its inner ring orange, and its central tea-leaf symbol navy. The short stalk connecting the central leaf toward the outer ring is orange, so connected parts must not all acquire one color. The orange stalk, navy leaf and both ring boundaries are clear, with no extra color bands.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. A normally placed running shoe presents its tongue toward the camera. A large tongue emblem consists of an orange solid lightning bolt passing through a navy ring. The short segment of the ring crossing the bolt stays navy; the remaining visible bolt inside and outside the ring stays orange. Only navy and orange inks occur in the emblem, without a third overlap color or an entirely navy bolt.

A close frontal photograph of a working vessel signal mast against pale sky. One vertical halyard holds exactly three separate matte-black day shapes: a ball at the top, a diamond made from two cones joined base to base in the middle, and a ball at the bottom. Clear sky separates the three bodies. The cone bases meet at the widest middle waist; their tips point away from each other.

A frontal close photograph of 2 clearly separate signal halyards on working vessels. Reading each from top to bottom and groups from left to right, the bodies are ball, two cones joined base to base, ball; upward cone, ball, downward cone. All bodies are matte black, physically separate with sky gaps, and every halyard has clear vessel ownership. No shapes from different groups share a cord.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. A close dockside photograph shows a working boat deck and its low mast. The mast suspends three separated black day shapes vertically: ball, diamond, ball from top to bottom. A short right-hand mast outrigger suspends just two separated black balls. They are actual three-dimensional hanging shapes, proportionate to the vessel, not symbols printed on a board, and do not obscure each other.

A frontal close photograph of 2 clearly separate signal halyards on working vessels. Reading each from top to bottom and groups from left to right, the bodies are ball, two cones joined base to base, ball; ball, ball. All bodies are matte black, physically separate with sky gaps, and every halyard has clear vessel ownership. No shapes from different groups share a cord.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. A physical harbor signal frame suspends one black day-shape group: an upward-pointing cone at the top, a ball in the middle and a downward-pointing cone at the bottom. Clear air gaps separate adjacent bodies. Do not merge the two cones into a diamond or replace the ball with a flat disc. The harbor building is background, with no second signal group.

A frontal close photograph of 2 clearly separate signal halyards on working vessels. Reading each from top to bottom and groups from left to right, the bodies are ball, ball; two cones joined base to base. All bodies are matte black, physically separate with sky gaps, and every halyard has clear vessel ownership. No shapes from different groups share a cord.

A frontal close photograph of 1 clearly separate signal halyards on working vessels. Reading each from top to bottom and groups from left to right, the bodies are upward cone, downward cone, ball. All bodies are matte black, physically separate with sky gaps, and every halyard has clear vessel ownership. No shapes from different groups share a cord.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. A barrel-shaped buoy beside a dock exposes its full upper body. Four equally broad vertical bands run down the visible camera-facing half, red, white, red, white from left to right. A single red spherical topmark stands above it. Do not turn the body bands horizontal or turn the ball into a cone. Water does not hide the relevant bands.

A frontal dockside photograph of two full-size navigation buoys on separate maintenance cradles. The left body has red, green and red horizontal bands from top to bottom and one red cylindrical topmark. The right has green, red and green bands and one green cone pointing upward. Both entire bodies and topmarks are large, separate and unobscured. No written navigation codes appear.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. One complete buoy stands upright in a dock maintenance area. Its body has three broad horizontal bands, black, yellow, black from top to bottom. Above it are two separate black cones: upper apex up, lower apex down, with their bases facing each other. Both the bands and cones are clear. Do not substitute yellow-black-yellow or make the cone tips point toward each other.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. An everyday soft first-aid pouch has one large embroidered badge: two pale palms cradle a red heart from the lower left and right. A single diagonal white bandage crosses the heart, with one short transverse seam at each end. The heart retains both upper lobes and its lower point. Do not let the palms replace the heart point or turn the bandage into a cross.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. A normally upright rain boot has a large side mark: a blue droplet outline encloses a white boot silhouette. The toe points right and the shaft is upright. The droplet tip is above the shaft and its bottom below the sole. Two short blue wave marks lie only in the blank interior below the boot sole, not through the white boot or outside the droplet.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. The back of a postcard has one large floral postage stamp at the upper right. Half of a circular postmark lies over the stamp’s left half and half over the surrounding paper; its only token is AIR. Three parallel straight cancellation strokes leave the right of the circle across the stamp’s right half. Only the lowest stroke continues into the blank paper below the stamp; the other two end to the right of the stamp. The strokes do not cross each other.

A natural, clear product photograph with complete readable working faces and an unobstructive setting. The flat top of a paper parcel bears two adjacent postage stamps with large mountain and boat motifs. One circular cancellation mark sits to their left; its right rim overlaps the left edge of the mountain stamp. Three parallel black wavy lines extend from the right of the circle, continue across both stamps and end beyond them. Keep exactly three continuous waves across the stamp boundaries, without breaks or restarts. The circle contains only the large token SEP.

A close photograph of a postal cancellation on an envelope: one complete black circular postmark at left, with three separate gently wavy black cancellation lines extending from its right rim. They meet the circle at upper-right, rightmost and lower-right locations without crossing inside it. Inside the circle is one large A only. No date, fine text or additional stamp.

A straight-on architectural photograph of a restaurant entrance with one large matte metal sign reading EVE. In the first E, the bottom horizontal stroke is the longest, the top stroke is intermediate, and the middle stroke is the shortest. In the final E, the middle horizontal stroke is the longest, the bottom stroke is intermediate, and the top stroke is the shortest. Each E has one straight vertical stem, and all three horizontal strokes extend rightward from that stem. Make the length differences generous and unmistakable, not typographic hairlines. The V is a conventional upright V. Keep all three glyphs separate and fully visible. No diagram or measurements printed on the sign.

A front-facing two-row shop wordmark has E F H F above and L E T L below, with letters colored blue, red, green and purple from left to right in each row. One broad opaque structural band spans between the rows. Its top edge is below the upper middle bars but above the upper bottom-bar level; its bottom edge is below the lower middle-bar level but above the lower bottom bars. Preserve all exposed stroke fragments and print nothing on the band.

A frontal close photograph of a shop-glass wordmark with two large block-letter rows. The upper row reads HKMRKMHR and the lower LEELEELL. One broad opaque metal guard strip between the rows covers only the lowest tips of the upper letters, leaving their characteristic middle strokes visible, and covers the upper portion of the lower letters so only bottom horizontal bars and left stems remain. The lower hidden letters need not be inferred: only exposed fragments are visible evidence. No duplicate words or printed explanations appear.

A straight-on close photograph of the cover of a flat hardcover book, off-white with four large dark-blue geometric letters in two aligned rows: P R above U J. P and R have identical upper parts, each with a left stem and rectangular upper bowl; R’s diagonal leg exists only in its lower half. U has two full stems joined by a bottom bar. J has a right stem, a bottom bar extending left, and a short upward hook at its left end, not a full left stem. One plain opaque brown paper belly band wraps across the whole book, covering the lower halves of the upper letters and the upper halves of the lower letters. Its top edge lies below both upper bowl bottoms but above the start of R’s leg. Its bottom edge is above the bottom bars of U and J. The exposed upper P and R fragments therefore match. Below the band, U shows two long lower stems and its bottom bar, while J shows a long right lower stem, bottom bar and a short left hook ending clearly below the band. All blue ink belongs to the cover, never the band. Do not move or shrink letters to evade occlusion.

A frontal close photograph of a shop glass door with two large evenly spaced rows of upright sans-serif block capitals. The upper row is FHFHEFHF and the lower row LTLTELLT. A single broad opaque horizontal door rail lies between the row centers: it hides the lower halves of the upper letters and the upper halves of the lower letters, including the center bars of H and E. Above the rail, the H letters show two separate upright strokes while E and F show a left upright joined to a top bar. Below the rail, T shows only its vertical stem while L and E show a stem joined to a bottom bar. These fragments remain large and distinct. Lettering exists on the glass behind the rail, never on its surface. No full letters are repeated elsewhere and no extra row or direction marker.

A frontal close photograph of a shop window with two large lines of heavy geometric block lettering. The upper line is HKMRKMHR and the lower line is LEELEELL. A single opaque horizontal metal protection strip lies between the lines. Its upper edge cuts through only the lowest part of the upper letters, leaving their distinguishing crossbars, diagonals and upper bowls visible. Its lower edge covers the upper portion of the lower letters, leaving only the bottom horizontal bars and their attached left vertical stems visible. The metal strip is one continuous physical piece. All exposed strokes are large and sharp; no duplicate words or printed explanations appear.

An overhead photograph of one large five-point star birthday cookie with a point upward. A complete dark-icing A at its center is half-turned relative to the star: its apex points down and its two feet up, with the crossbar belonging to that inverted A. Keep icing clear of cookie edges. Do not rotate the whole cookie or add direction labels.

Frontal close photograph of a wide sneaker tongue carrying one M-shaped bold polyline: lower-left to upper-left to a right-offset valley to upper-right to lower-right. Put arrowheads only midway along segment two pointing down-right, segment three up-right, and the final vertical pointing upward, against the left-to-right traversal. The valley is above both feet; outer tops level. Keep heads away from vertices.

Frontal photograph of a thick card stencil with one large N cutout revealing yellow paper behind. Its two vertical openings are equally wide and clearly wider than the diagonal opening, which joins upper-left to lower-right. Intact outer card border and visible cut edges; no printed yellow N substitute.

Frontal photograph of a matte seven-point metal star brooch with one point upward and seven clear outer tips/valleys. Its center contains an N cutout revealing dark cloth: equal broad uprights and a narrower descending-right diagonal. Intact outer star, no printed black-letter substitute or extra sparkle points.

An overhead close photograph of a packaging print proof. Two broad ink rectangles overlap, producing three adjacent visible vertical fields: cyan on the left, deep blue in the overlap, magenta on the right. One continuous cream paper-colored capital E is knocked out across all three fields. Its left vertical stem is in cyan; each of its three horizontal arms crosses the blue overlap into magenta. No colored E is added on top, no arm is filled in, and no duplicate letter appears.

Overhead photograph of a flat color-block apron, navy on the left and ivory on the right. One large R spans the vertical seam: ivory ink on navy cloth, navy ink on ivory cloth. Its upper bowl and diagonal leg each continue geometrically across the seam while only their color reverses. The stem stays left; the leg extends farther right than the bowl. No duplicated R.

A frontal photograph of a metal coffee-shop monogram combining a normal P on the right and a mirrored P on the left. They share one central vertical stem. Their upper bowls have equal height, but the left bowl is narrower. The lower stem remains single and unbranched. Do not make two separate Ps.

Front-facing product photo of an ivory carton printed with a thick blue rectangular border and a red H centered inside. A vertical kraft sealing strip covers the middle of the border’s top and bottom edges. A rectangular window in the strip fully exposes the red H. The H touches none of the border edges, and no blue ink is added onto the sealing strip to restore the hidden border.

An overhead close photograph of a wooden-handled cookie stamp lying with its working face upward beside one intact solid butter biscuit. The stamp bears a raised backward capital F: its stem is on the right, with a long upper bar and shorter lower bar extending left. The biscuit bears the corresponding recessed upright F, stem at left and bars extending right, upper longer than lower. Every groove has biscuit material at its bottom, never an opening through to the counter. No holes or extra lettering on the stamp.

Overhead photograph of a flat zipped sports jacket with one bold N across the center zipper. The left upright is shorter than the right, with level bottoms. The diagonal descends from the left upright top to the right upright bottom and continues in register across the zipper. The right upright extends higher alone. Do not mirror the halves or reverse the diagonal.

Frontal photograph of one layered paper A sculpture: large blue rear, ivory middle, smaller red front. Left feet align vertically; apices shift right from rear to front. Crossbars slope up-right, level, and down-right respectively. Leave narrow separation edges and keep all key strokes visible. Do not split into three side-by-side letters.

A frontal photograph of one complete metal A. The two feet share one horizontal baseline and the apex stays upright. Its crossbar slopes upward from left to right and joins both legs; the counter’s lower boundary follows that sloping bar. Do not tilt the entire A or restore a horizontal crossbar. Use a broad readable counter and strokes, without dimension lines.

A frontal photograph of a stationery-shop metal QQ wordmark with two equal-sized separate Qs. The left Q’s diagonal tail begins inside its counter, crosses the lower-right outer contour and extends outside. The right Q’s tail remains entirely inside the counter and does not touch the outer contour. Both tails point down-right and remain thick and clear. Do not turn the right Q into a tailless O.

Frontal photograph of a three-piece record sleeve with two vertical joins. One large R spans the cover: stem on the left piece, broad shallow upper bowl crossing only the left join, and a long down-right leg crossing both joins to end on the right piece. Keep stroke registration at joins. Do not center a normal typeface independently on the pieces. No title.

A near-overhead photograph of an open lettering workbook with a shallow angle at the binding. One large Z spans the spread, its diagonal continuing across the spine. The bottom bar is longer than the top and extends farther right. Do not write a separate Z on each page or equalize the two bars. Keep pages and ink unobstructed.

A frontal photograph of one square patchwork cushion whose few large fabric pieces collectively carry one dark S. The S continues in register across seams. Its upper bend is wider than its lower bend, with open stroke ends. Do not split it into several small letters or equalize both bends. Keep the cushion flat and unobstructed.

A frontal photograph of one large wooden W on a shop wall. Its outer upper endpoints share one height; the middle upper peak is lower. Its right valley is lower than its left valley. Four continuous equal-thickness diagonals form the W. Do not regularize it into a standard symmetric W. Show only this one complete prominent wordmark.

Frontal photograph of five touching hardcover spines carrying one large continuous M across the set. Its outer uprights have equal height; its central valley lies right of center and above both upright bottoms. The left diagonal crosses the first and second seams; the right diagonal crosses the third and fourth seams, continuing in register. No complete M on any individual spine and no other lettering.

Frontal photograph of closed shop double doors with one large high-contrast frosted W. The door seam cuts the middle descending-right stroke, not a peak or valley. The left valley is deeper than the right, and the central upper peak is below both outer endpoints. Continue strokes across the seam. Do not print two Vs or snap vertices to the seam. Quiet background.

Overhead photograph of a three-key macro pad, one broad upper key above two narrower lower keys. One large R spans all three: its upper bowl crosses the horizontal key seam, its descending leg crosses the lower vertical seam, and its left stem stays continuous. No repeated R per key or bowl confined to the upper key.

Near-normal overhead photograph of a complete four-key macro pad. Its four square keycaps jointly form one large Y. The upper diagonals span the two top keys; their junction lies inside the lower-left key, not at the four-key seam intersection, and the stem continues downward in the lower row. Continue strokes across seams. No separate Y per key or extra text.

A near-frontal interior photograph of a three-panel folding screen with shallow side angles and all front faces visible. Dark painted strokes across the panels form one complete large K in this view. Its two diagonals meet the same vertical stem midpoint without restarting at folds. Do not print one K per panel. Frame the complete screen compactly in diffuse light with no strong perspective.

A close frontal bookshelf photo of three broad adjacent hardbacks sharing one large N across their dust jackets: a left vertical, a diagonal descending left-to-right across all three spines, and a right vertical. The lower half of the middle jacket folds forward, carrying the middle diagonal segment onto that flap and exposing a plain spine beneath. Both outer books stay unchanged. The segment on the flap remains oblique, not a new letter or a horizontal stripe.

Front-on storefront photograph with four equal-width sans-serif letters EFEF, blue, red, green, purple. In every letter the left stem, top bar and middle bar have matching positions and lengths; only E has a bottom bar. A solid lower structural beam fully hides the bottom-bar level and everything below it but leaves the middle bars visible. The four exposed silhouettes are therefore identical.
